history.prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph of heavy, cream-colored financial documents and embossed vesting certificates arranged on a dark leather desk blotter. The papers are fanned out to reveal exactly six distinct staggered layers or tranches. Top-down 90-degree view, even diffused daylight with a single warm focused desk lamp casting soft directional shadows across the textured paper stock. One document is slightly out of alignment to look handled. Blank and illegibly cropped paper, muted paper tones, minimalist, premium editorial aesthetic, shallow depth of field on the top sheet.

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a real textured surface. Six sequential interlocking inspection gates arranged in a deliberate staggered, cascading sequence, representing distinct operational tranches. The assembly is anchored by heavy asymmetrical framing off-centre on the right third, leaving generous empty negative space on the left. Constructed with hard clean edges from matte dark polymer and frosted copper, resting on a weathered brushed steel bench. One dramatic directional light throwing a long, distinct cast shadow. Muted modern premium editorial palette, high-end industrial hardware design.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, wordmarks, signage, UI, labels, watermarks, logos
rationale: A component assembly perfectly visualizes the abstract concept of 'six windows' and 'staggered lockups' as a tangible, engineered sequence. The physical modularity emphasizes the deliberate, tranche-by-tranche nature of the equity schedule.
subject: six sequential interlocking modular inspection gates in a staggered configuration
core_thesis: A staged IPO lockup forces employees to engineer their equity strategy across six distinct tranches rather than a single sell-or-hold cliff.
core_conflict: Sequential liquidity windows vs standardized tax and trading schedules
